item.title: New MVA Course on Language Models and Transformers Launches in Fall 2026
item.description:
New MVA Course on Language Models and Transformers Launches in Fall 2026

The Master Vision Apprentissage (MVA) program is introducing a new course focused on language models and transformers during the first semester of the academic year 2026–2027. Taught in English, the course is open to all students enrolled in the MVA program and is structured around eight sessions held between October and December 2026.

David Louapre and Nathanaël Fijalkow lead the first four sessions, covering foundational topics in language modeling, transformer architectures, pre-training dynamics, and post-training alignment. Each session provides educational materials including slides in PDF or HTML format, lecture notes, and interactive Jupyter notebooks. Additional sessions in November and December are scheduled, with further details on content and resources to be released.

A companion course is offered in the second semester by Marc Lelarge and Guillaume Baudart, titled Large Language Models for Code and Proof.

📚 Course Structure

Session Date Instructor Topic Resources
1 October 1 David Louapre Language models Slides (PDF), Hugging Face Space
2 October 29 Nathanaël Fijalkow Transformers Slides (HTML), Lecture notes, Notebook
3 November 5 David Louapre Pre-training and scaling laws Slides (PDF), Slides (PDF)
4 November 12 Nathanaël Fijalkow Post-training and alignment Slides (HTML), Lecture notes, Notebook, Recording (passcode: =S3^kc2U)
5 November 19 David Louapre Decoding and inference optimization Slides (PDF)
6 November 26 Nathanaël Fijalkow Advanced architectures Slides (HTML), Lecture notes, Notebook

🛠️ Resource Format and Tools

All lecture materials are built from source files using Quarto, a markdown-based publishing system. The course repository includes:

  • Source files in src/ folder, with each lecture defined in a .qmd file that generates slides, notes, and notebooks.
  • Supporting assets in figs/ and anim/ directories.
  • A render.py script to compile individual or multiple lectures. Run with python3 render.py 01 06 to build lectures 1 and 6.
  • Use python3 render.py 01 --slides to generate only the slides for lecture 1.

The notebooks are executable and designed to run the lab component of each lecture. Execution is cached and only re-runs when code cells change, which may take several minutes.

🗓️ Timeline

  • Course runs during the first semester of the MVA academic year 2026–2027 (October–January 2027).
  • Sessions are held weekly from October through December 2026.
  • A second course, Large Language Models for Code and Proof, begins in the second semester of 2026–2027.

💬 Why It Matters

The course introduces students to core concepts in modern language modeling, including the evolution from early NLP to large language models (LLMs), the mechanics of transformers, and practical aspects of model training and deployment. Emphasis is placed on hands-on learning through notebooks and real-world tools like Hugging Face Spaces.

Students will also explore advanced topics such as agent design and alignment techniques, preparing them for current developments in AI systems.

#MLCourse #Transformers #LargeLanguageModels #AIAlignment #MVA

item.title: Datawhale China Releases Alpha Version of Embodied AI Learning Platform with Online Simulation
item.description:
Datawhale China Releases Alpha Version of Embodied AI Learning Platform with Online Simulation

Datawhale China has launched an alpha internal test version of “Dive into Embodied AI” (具身智能), a comprehensive learning platform for embodied intelligent robot development. The platform covers the full “decision—control—perception” pipeline using reinforcement learning, world models, and VLA (Vision-Language-Action) methods across simulation environments, controllers, motion planning, and perception systems.

🔍 Overview

The platform is structured into four main sections:

  • Embodied Introduction (具身导论): Field overview with curated papers, datasets, open-source projects, and tools
  • Theoretical Foundation (理论基础): Core principles and concepts
  • Project Practice (项目实战): Hands-on projects organized by AMD Zone, Simulation Practice, and Real Machine Practice
  • Online Simulation (在线仿真): Interactive browser-based simulation environment

The release is labeled as an alpha internal test version, currently undergoing migration and restructuring with some chapters as placeholder pages. Users are encouraged to submit issues for feedback.

🧩 How it works

Online Simulation Features

The simulation environment (accessible at https://datawhalechina.github.io/dive-into-embodied-ai/simulation) provides:

  • Two modes: game-style free manipulation and policy demonstration
  • Pre-loaded policies:
    • Go2 and Pupper v3 PPO walking policies
    • Quaddle periodic gait comparison
    • MicroDuck head and full-body joint free manipulation (walking weights not yet available)
  • Controls: keyboard and on-screen directional buttons, pause, reset, slow simulation, camera follow
  • Go2 displays with simplified appearance using original collision model

Curriculum Structure

Embodied Introduction (7 chapters):

  1. What is Embodied AI — definition, perception-decision-action loop, body importance
  2. Development History — rule programming, model control, deep RL, and large model eras
  3. Robot Skills — tasks, grasping, manipulation, locomotion, navigation
  4. Embodied Carriers — humanoid, robotic arms, wheeled, quadruped, mobile manipulation, simulation bodies
  5. Core Challenges — data, sim-to-real, generalization, real-time, safety, evaluation
  6. Tech Stack — VLM, VLA, world models, manipulation, control, navigation modules
  7. Career Roles — brain algorithms, cerebellum algorithms, perception/navigation, engineering platforms, hardware

Project Practice Categories:

Category Projects
AMD Zone AUP Learning Cloud (Ryzen AI APU, ROCm, JupyterHub, Code Server); MicroDuck RL on AMD ROCm (R9700, ROCm MuJoCo Warp, dynamic contact regression, bipedal PPO); Pupper Quadruped on AMD (RL locomotion policies, VLA experiments)
Simulation Practice Build Quadruped from Scratch (MuJoCo, PD, kinematics, policy training, language control, perception); Petoi Quaddle Servo Walking (official URDF, alternating gait, contact verification, infinite checkerboard); MicroDuck RL (mjlab + MuJoCo Warp, GPU parallel PPO, bipedal gait); MuJoCo Arm with DDPG; ACT Bimanual Manipulation (ACT + ALOHA training, evaluation, reproduction)
Real Machine Practice LeRobot Chinese Course (Units 0-2: robot learning, datasets, toolchain, classic robotics); SO-101 + LeRobot Real Machine Tutorial (hardware connection, safety testing, action replay)

🚀 Availability

  • Platform language support: Chinese, English, Italian
  • Alpha version — active migration and restructuring in progress
  • Some chapters are placeholder pages
  • Model library integration planned (see simulation/README.md)
  • Tutorial and interactive pages include “Copy as Markdown” with Markdown preview dropdown

💡 Why it matters

This platform provides an end-to-end educational resource bridging theory and practice for embodied AI development, with particular emphasis on hardware-accessible projects (AMD ROCm support, real robot tutorials) and interactive browser-based simulation for immediate experimentation without local GPU setup.

#EmbodiedAI #Robotics #ReinforcementLearning #VLA #MuJoCo #Datawhale

item.title: Launch of the Get Shit Done with AI Bootcamp
item.description:
Launch of the Get Shit Done with AI Bootcamp

The AI Engineering Academy has introduced the “Get Shit Done with AI” Bootcamp, a self-paced program focused on real-world applications designed to equip students with the skills to become AI engineers.

🔍 Overview

The bootcamp covers a broad spectrum of AI development, ranging from core code and machine learning fundamentals to the deployment of generative AI applications.

⚙️ Key Details

Technical Curriculum

  • Language & Data Essentials: Python data structures, functional tricks, typing, JSON, pathlib, NumPy, and Pandas.
  • Mathematical Foundations: Linear algebra, calculus, and probability.
  • Machine Learning Fundamentals: Linear regression (feature scaling to evaluation) and PyTorch (tensors, autograd, data loading, optimizers, and training loops).
  • Generative AI & LLMs: Tutorials on Ollama, LLMs, RAGs, LangChain, LangGraph, Fine-tuning, DSPy, and AI Agents (CrewAI).
  • Supported Models: ChatGPT, gpt-oss, Claude, Qwen, Gemma, Llama, and Gemini.

Production & Deployment

  • Data Engineering: Data exploration using Pandas and Seaborn (Bank Marketing dataset), data validation with pandera, feature engineering with scikit-learn Pipelines, and versioning with DVC.
  • MLOps: Experiment tracking with MLflow and tuning LightGBM models.
  • Shipping: Building REST APIs with FastAPI and packaging applications into Docker containers.
  • Cloud Deployment: Pushing artifacts to S3, storing images in ECR, and orchestrating deployment via AWS ECS and EC2.

🚀 Availability

Interested individuals can access the program through the following channels:

  • AI Engineering Academy
  • Discord community
  • YouTube channel

#AIEngineering #MachineLearning #GenerativeAI #MLOps #PyTorch
